newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen up on crude gains, demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen up on crude gains, demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were assessed higher on good buying interest and crude gains, traders said.
High sulphur, 180 centistoke-grade fuel oil prices took a turn late Wednesday to edge up higher to $117-$118 per tonne for end November/early December lifting.
Traders said prices were expected to continue to climb on good buying interest. They said a trader who were buying on Wednesday remained a keen buyer on Thursday.
The local trader purchased a total of two 20,000-tonne cargoes of fuel oil from a European refiner and a local oil firm at $117.50 and $117 respectively.

A Japanese trader said Chinese buyers have emerged to buy December-arrival barrels. The trader said that he had sold cargoes at "just under $8.00 per tonne premium" to Singapore spot quotes c-and-f southern China.
Traders said South Korean supplies in December were usual despite refiners there reporting lower fuel oil production while boosting middle distillates for winter stockpile.

But some traders remained bearish, citing a slight build in fuel oil stocks in Singapore of around 240,000 barrels to 11.614 million barrels. In the swaps market, November was quoted at $117-$118 per tonne, up $1.50 from Wednesday.
